chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the man who forgets the Adhan and the Iqamah until he enters into the Salat, he (peace be upon him) said: If he remembered before he recited, let him send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and let him recite the Iqamah; and if he had already recited, let him complete his Salat.

key_terms.الْإِقَامَة: Iqamah (Second Call to Prayer, establishing the prayer)
key_terms.يَقْرَأ: He recites (referring to the recitation of Quran in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget the Iqamah call before starting their prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural flexibility in the call to prayer, ruling that the Iqamah is not a strict prerequisite for the validity of the prayer itself but rather a recommended act to be performed before the recitation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the essential pillars of Salah and the supplementary sunnahs, emphasizing that forgetting the Iqamah does not invalidate the worship if the prayer has already commenced. It reflects the practical ease (taysir) intended by the Imams in ritual observance.
